title: How on earth David Fincher hasn't won Oscar yet?

commenti.body: The social network was the one. In most other years he would have bagged his Oscar there but the kings speech really had some legs to it but afterwards nobody brings it up. Nothing against kings speech but I don’t know anybody who watched it more than once or after the Oscar’s that year whereas social network holds up remarkably well.

Fincher is my favourite director. The Social Network and The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo are technical masterpieces. He is a perfectionist and it shows. These movies are flawless. I think academy will award him an Oscar in his late career, as an apology. For much inferior film of his career.
I'm looking forward to watch The Girl With Dragon Tattoo. The rating is good.
Aaron Sorkin's script was top notch.
But I'm still happy that Trent Reznor won the oscar for the soundtrack.

I think I would have enjoyed his Girl with the Dragon Tattoo more had I not already seen the 2009 extended films. The American one paled in comparison despite it being well directed and scored. 

The Social Network 100% should have won over The Kings Speech.

You could make a very long list of people who deserve an Oscar but haven't gotten one.  There just aren't enough Oscars to go around for all of the talented people out there.  Scorsese didn't get one until 2007, for The Departed, and look at all the amazing work he did for decades before that.  Oscars don't mean anything.

You still didn't watch The Game, OP. My favorite of his next to Se7en. His career as a music video director is also underrated, I love his "Bad Girl" video for Madonna.

And, I don't know... the Oscars are a popularity contest between academy members mostly. I've already abandoned the idea that Oscar wins are solely based on a film's qualities. David Fincher seems to me to tackle subject that might be considered a bit crass to more conservative voters (the serial killer in Zodiac, the gruesome murders in Se7en, etc.) and, though I never read deeply about his thoughts on this, it seems he's not a director who made any of his films with too much thirst for an Oscar, and it's fine. His good films will win the test of time, with or without an Oscar.

1. The Oscars aren't exactly the greatest indicator of quality in a movie. I don't need to explain this, just open the Wikipedia page for any Oscar ceremony and look at the winners and nominees.

2. I don't know if you watch soccer/football, but an Oscar is like a Ballon d'Or: maybe that year you did a great performance, but you were just unlucky because there was someone who ourclassed you. And the next year it's possible that the one who wins the award does a shitty performance, but because the level is lower in general he still wins.

So, I guess a mix of lack of consideration, incompetence and bad luck.

The Oscars are basically a popularity and agenda pushing ceremony that doesn't necessarily decide what the best movie of the year was. Also, hes a good director, but, at least in my opinion, outside of the social network, nothing hes made has really been that deserving of an "oscar" tbh.
